BREAKING: @FoxNews has obtained a memo that AG Todd Blanche sent out to DOJ this afternoon announcing that DOJ will be surging lawyers and resources to jurisdictions that have been overwhelmed by habeas corpus petitions filed by illegal aliens and their lawyers after their ICE arrests.

A habeas petition is a request to a federal judge to determine if detention is unlawful. These requests are handled by federal judges, not immigration judges, and DOJ feels many of the claims are “frivolous” and get put in the hands of activist/sympathetic judges, and the petitions are an effort by immigration lawyers and activists to thwart enforcement of U.S. immigration law.

Nearly 100,000 of these habeas petitions have been filed since the start of the Trump admin, and aliens have been successful in using them to get released from ICE custody after arrest.

Some US Attorney Office have reportedly been so overwhelmed by these petitions, they are sometimes unable to send anyone to court to challenge them. 

With this memo, AG Blanche appears to be telling DOJ help is coming - and these petitions will be fought in court to advance President Trump’s immigration enforcement agents.

Fox is told the most overwhelmed districts have been: 

Central District of California 
Eastern District of California 
Western District of Texas 
Southern District of Texas 
New Jersey 
Colorado 
Western District of Washington

posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 This war was supposed to last 2-4 weeks. In February, it turns one year old.

Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Endowment and fmr. State Dept. analyst and negotiator, joins to discuss.

His central point: nobody is looking for an off-ramp.

Can Trump walk away? Miller says no.

Walking away from a war that failed every objective, and may have accelerated Iran's nuclear program rather than preventing it, isn't a legacy he can absorb.

The June 17th MOU made it worse. Miller's verdict after 20 years negotiating in the region: it was a giveaway of extraordinary dimension, front-loaded in Iran's favor.

A deal is theoretically possible. But pain and gain have to balance on both sides before anyone moves.

Meanwhile, the Houthis are striking Riyadh's financial center. Saudi Vision 2030, the investment pitch, the tourism, the data centers. All of it now fundamentally at risk.

There is no military solution. The U.S. launched over a thousand strikes on Houthi targets last year. It barely made a dent.

The Gulf states are the real losers. Sandwiched between an aggressive Iran and Houthis who control up to 15% of global seaborne trade through the Gate of Tears. 

Angry at the U.S., yet dependent on it.

It won't end conclusively. It never does in this region. But it could be de-escalated, managed, set in a different direction.

Miller just doesn't see anyone with the will to do it.

@aarondmiller2

Together with Hungarian Prime Minister @magyarpeterMP, we visited the Lajos Kossuth Lyceum in Berehove. We spoke with students and teachers and played volleyball with the children.

This is a modern school with a history spanning more than a century, attended by over 500 children, including those in inclusive classrooms. Classes are taught in Hungarian, but students also learn Ukrainian and English. Similarly, there is a school in Budapest where Ukrainian children study in their native language. This kind of mutual respect is important for our relations, and it must be the foundation of all our cooperation.

Despite the war, the lyceum continues to develop. Classrooms are being renovated, and children have every opportunity to learn, grow, and play sports. I thank the teachers who make this possible. And, of course, thanks to both teams for a great game!
